title: Particle effects with a fixed budget
when: The game wants sparks, smoke, explosions or trails that look rich but must never grow memory or frame time without bound.
prompt:
Goal: A pooled particle system with a hard cap that degrades gracefully on slow devices.
Steps:
1. MAX = 600; store fields in typed arrays allocated once: Float32Array for x, y, vx, vy, life, maxLife, size and Uint8Array for kind.
2. emit(kind, x, y, count) fills free slots; when the pool is full it skips the rest, never allocating.
3. update(dt): life -= dt, apply velocity and drag, and when life <= 0 copy the last alive slot into this one so alive particles stay packed.
4. Draw grouped by kind with one fillStyle each, globalAlpha = life / maxLife, and small fillRect calls instead of arc for sparks.
5. Use globalCompositeOperation = "lighter" only for glow kinds and set it back to "source-over" after.
6. Quality scale: when the average frame time over 60 frames passes 18 ms halve emit counts; restore slowly when under 12 ms.
7. Cut counts to a quarter when prefers-reduced-motion matches.
Quality bar:
- The system creates no objects per frame; the memory graph stays flat.
- A 200 particle explosion updates in under 1 ms on a laptop.
Pitfalls:
- Array.splice on dead particles, which is slow and makes garbage.
- shadowBlur on many particles, which is very expensive.
- Forgetting to reset globalAlpha, fading the whole HUD.
Verify:
- [ ] Spamming explosions keeps the alive count at or under MAX.
- [ ] Frame time stays steady during a big burst.
Output: js/particles.js exporting emit, update, draw and setQuality.

examples.input: explosões com partículas sem deixar o jogo lento
examples.output: typed array pool of 600, packed removal, grouped draws, adaptive quality, reduced motion cut
